target.title: Add secure bridge artifact transfer
target.body:
## Summary

- transfer ChatGPT-generated files from a browser bridge host back to the client through a token-protected pull endpoint
- advertise protocol support and size limits through `/health` capability negotiation
- sanitize filenames and verify byte count, SHA-256, and ZIP structure with bounded reads before publishing client-local artifacts
- serialize same-name artifact allocation so concurrent bridge events cannot overwrite or deduplicate files
- preserve text responses and provide a manual-copy fallback for mixed-version or failed transfers
- expose validation and transfer metadata in stored sessions and bridge diagnostics

## Security

The NDJSON result contains only minimal redacted descriptors. It does not expose host filesystem paths, ChatGPT cookies, bridge credentials, signed download URLs, host-only labels, or host-only warnings. The host registers only real files beneath Oracle session artifact directories. Artifact fetches reuse the existing bridge bearer token, reject malformed identifiers, stream through a fixed byte limit, validate ZIP headers and the bounded end-of-file directory window, and expire from the host registry after a bounded TTL.

## Validation

- exact candidate: `f5a1d1ae0976fc0926472fd3a64c12d5a6f86db6`
- `pnpm run check`
- `pnpm run build`
- `pnpm run docs:check && pnpm run docs:site`
- focused bridge/browser tests: 52 passed
- full unit suite: 1,377 passed, 43 skipped
- full-branch autoreview: clean with no actionable findings
- exact-head cross-host live proof: macOS bridge host to Ubuntu 25.10 arm64 client using packed candidate `c7abc5b0bd00d38288e3f5e5587047be2180259388092a480eaaa62ea26c658c`
- live ChatGPT Pro generated `oracle-pr277-proof.zip`; the bridge delivered the 250-byte client-local ZIP with SHA-256 `ce772c6a037ce5bf9c556eca4fd4c82c7afb0b09109b24d1ab8fcb16fa9f5c54`, valid central directory, and exact `a.txt` / `b.txt` markers
- duplicate-name cross-host transfer preserved both files as `oracle-pr277-proof.zip` and `oracle-pr277-proof-2.zip` without overwrite; both matched the source hash and contents
- unauthenticated cross-host health request returned 401; returned metadata and client session state contained no host-local path, backend URL, bearer token, or signed download URL
